newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Sentiment to improve with cuts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Sentiment to improve with cuts.

text.p: Naphtha edged up amid firmer swaps and improved sentiment prompted by refinery run cuts, traders said on Wednesday.
Naphtha July swaps firmed by 15 cents per barrel to $20.60/$20.70 per barrel, brokers said.
A cut in Singapore supplies of light distillates are likely to support prices, they said.
Shell Singapore has cut crude runs to 50,000 tonnes-per-day (TPD) at its 59,000-TPD (435,000-barrel-per-day) refinery following poor margins and high stocks, a spokeswoman said.
She also said that the company has scheduled a one-week maintenance for its No. 4 115,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) begining on July 6.
Industry sources said Exxon Singapore has also cut crude runs by about 10 percent since late last month but this was not confirmed by company officials.

Bids into Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp's (CPC) July light naphtha sell tender improved with the best bid from Dutch trader Vitol at 53 cents per barrel below Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board Colombo basis, a CPC official said.
The tender which offered 125,000 barrels of light naphtha lifting July 18-19 lifting, closed on July 2 but bids will be valid for two days.
CPC's last tender award was much lower at a $1.23 per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, for May 2-3 lifting, fob Colombo.
The gasoline market was extremely quiet with only a bid heard on the swaps market for August at $23.20 per barrel, up from $23.05.
Traders said they expected the lull in the market to continue until the award of the Taiwan import tender for second-half August, closing July 9 and valid for two days.
